Details

Days are days of beam per µA to reach 3σ at the ATOMKI strength (R = 5.8 × 10⁻⁶, statistics only, Asimov fit in θ × |y| × n_down), MX17 with the big plastics, E_p = 1.10 MeV. Time scales as 1/current.

"Material per lepton" is the median x/X₀ crossed by an X17 lepton on its way to the arms, from one ray-trace applied to every design in the same way (opt_sketch.py). It ranks the designs; it is not Geant4.

Ten designs: the Be ogive leads, the window on a Be tube and the flat target follow, the Cu shells trail ×11

Flat target in a chamber

one 200 µm Cu wall, square on (1.4 %)

+ for

  • the best resolution of the flat stacks as simulated in L9 (6.6°); 8.3° with the 1 mm chamber
  • the target is not the vacuum wall: a crack does not vent the line
  • film and stack fully characterised (thermal model, L9)

− against

  • needs a CFRP chamber around the target (Pierfrancesco wants none); the 0.4 mm × 600 mm one of L9 would buckle at 0.35 bar, a buildable 1 mm × 300 mm chamber is run in L11 (§21)
  • Cu holder ring edge-on to the 75–90° legs (the tall bar)
  • heat leaves through a Cu arm to the chamber flange

3

Details

Geant4 run L9 (li20_mo8_dia50), big plastics, 1.10 MeV. The film is perpendicular to the beam inside a CFRP chamber (0.4 mm, r 25 mm). This is "our perpendicular design".

On 24 Oct Pierfrancesco proposed making the target the end of the beam pipe, with no chamber. The diamond window is this same stack turned into that end wall. Sources: TARGET_OPTIONS §7, §14–16; SHAPES_GEANT.md §0.

Diamond window, 45°

one 200 µm Cu wall, square on (1.4 %)

+ for

  • no chamber: the window is the end of the vacuum
  • safe at 1 bar (Ø20, 200–300 µm diamond)
  • tilting moves the rings out of the 90° plane; spreads the spot ×√2

− against

  • the 0.5 mm Al end piece is grazed by legs at 90–140° (σ68 9.1° vs 6.2° without it)
  • Mo K x-rays (17.5 keV) through the diamond: 16 % MM occupancy per arm per µA (est.)
  • window = beam stop = vacuum wall: blistering or a crack vents the line (fast valve)

Diamond window, 45°

one 200 µm Cu wall, square on (1.4 %)

+ for

  • the end piece stays in the leptons’ view, but Be puts ×4 less material there than Al (0.14 % vs 0.56 % X₀)
  • a Ø20 × 0.5 mm Be tube is a catalogue beam-pipe part; it holds 1 bar with a margin of ~9
  • keeps every advantage of the window; nothing else changes

− against

  • Be: toxic dust when machined, brazed not glued, a specialist part (cost, lead time)
  • Mo K x-rays as for the window
  • the 0.25 mm Al end piece gets part of the way for free (diagnostic)

5

Details

Geant4 run L11 (win45be), big plastics, 1.10 MeV. Why the wall and not its shape: any closed vacuum envelope around a tilted window must cross the arms’ view on the downstream side of the tilt, and the solid angle it subtends from the vertex is the same for a Ø20 tube, a cone or a wide step (the window plane is the only radial surface). So the material in view can only be made thinner or lighter. Diagnostics (X17 only): Al 0.25 mm, CFRP 0.5 and 1 mm, a 16 mm Al end piece straight on the grey flange. SHAPES_GEANT.md §10.

Details

Geant4 run L11 (win45wide), big plastics, 1.10 MeV. This is the "open to ≥ Ø60 within a few mm" idea of SHAPES_GEANT.md §4.1, run in full. The wall a tilted window needs on its downstream side subtends the same solid angle whatever its radius; the plate (radial) costs little and the big tube costs what the small one did. §10.

Details

Cu ogive

one 200 µm Cu wall, square on (1.4 %)

+ for

  • steep walls everywhere: the 90° legs cross ≈ 1.1× the wall, not 10×
  • no flange in the arms’ view (base 63 mm back)
  • large area for air cooling

− against

  • still 200 µm of Cu on every lepton, and the Cu converts the ⁸Be γ (EPC 23% of the background)
  • the beam spot spills onto the 65° flank: 2.2× the Li along the path at 1.10 MeV, and the 17.64 MeV line becomes 28 % of γ₀ (69 % at 1.03)
  • the flank Li path makes the yields depend on the spot size and the film thickness there

10

Details

Geant4 run L11 (ogCu200), big plastics, 1.10 MeV: the exact CAD profile as G4Polycone layers (OgiveProfile.hh), vertices on the inner surface where the σ 2 mm spot lands (cap and flank). The yields fold the flank path (opt_sketch.ogive_yield_mix): γ₀ ×2.2 per proton at 1.10 MeV, of which 28 % is the 17.64 MeV line, counted as IPC background and not as signal. A bare-base diagnostic shows the mount is out of view. §10.

Be ogive

one 200 µm Cu wall, square on (1.4 %)

+ for

  • ×8 less material per lepton than in Cu, half the window; almost no γ conversion (EPC 2%)
  • no chamber, no tube in view
  • keeps the shell idea Pierfrancesco prefers; at 1 bar the 300 µm shell has ×20 margin (§20)

− against

  • a custom part from a Be shop: ~5–25 k€ each, months (ESTIMATE, ask for a quote)
  • needs LNL safety approval (EU carcinogen); brittle, so a failure leaves Be fragments in the line
  • the same 441 keV issue on the flank as the Cu ogive, unless the Li is masked to the tip; Mo K x-rays escape through the Be

11

Details

Geant4 run L11 (ogBe300mo8, 200 µm: ogBe200mo8), big plastics, 1.10 MeV, with the flank Li path folded in as for the Cu ogive. Material check (TARGET_OPTIONS §20, ESTIMATE): at 1 bar the 300 µm Be shell has ×20 margin on buckling and on stress (200 µm: ×7); the tip runs 41 K above the air at 4 µA with a fan; join it by a thick Be collar at the base, bonded by the vendor into a Ti/SS CF ring, 63 mm behind the tip and out of the arms’ view. §10, §20, §21.

Can we build it? Every design holds 1 bar and stays cool once three walls are thickened

Practical check per design (ESTIMATE): margin to failure at 1 bar, Li temperature rise at LNL's 4 µA, first-unit cost and lead time, difficulty 1–5 (hover a row for the parts)

Common to every design (not in the costs): Li evaporation at LNL; a fast-closing valve upstream (~5–10 k€ if LNL has none), because in every design the target or its chamber is the vacuum wall; 2–3 spare targets per campaign.

13

Details

Margin = failure pressure (buckling, with a knockdown: 0.56 for tubes and cones, 0.2 for spheres) or strength (yield; CVD diamond 280 MPa, the growth side in tension) over the 1 bar load. CERN practice asks ≥ 3 for buckling. "Simulated" is the geometry Geant4 ran; "to build" is the change recommended here. Li rise: the full heat path to the air at 4 µA (4.4 W at 1.10 MeV) with a fan (h = 100 W/m²/K); the Li must stay below ~150 °C. The 20 µm Li runs at 0.12–0.5 µA, ×8–30 less heat. Costs are first-unit ranges from public prices and quotes, not quotes (TARGET_OPTIONS §21; opt_practical.py).

Physics against practicality: the cheap, routine designs are also the fast ones

Each dot is a design (its colour as on the other slides); the bar is the cost range, coloured by difficulty (green routine, gold development, red specialist + approval). Lower-left is best.

difficulty 1–2

14

Details

Days per µA from the Geant4 runs of the deck (big plastics, 1.10 MeV). The Be variants buy little reach for ×3–10 the cost and a safety approval, so take them only if the cheaper version of the same idea is not enough. ESTIMATE costs (TARGET_OPTIONS §21).

Three of the simulated geometries must change before they are built

Closed-form shell, plate and fin estimates; the LNL mechanical office should confirm by FEA

Flat target: the CFRP chamber

0.4 mm × 600 mm, as in L9, buckles at 0.35 bar. Make it ≥ 1 mm and ≤ 300 mm long (×7). Cost to the leptons (trace): σ68 7.4° → 8.2°.

Windows: the diamond

200 µm over Ø20 carries 198 MPa at its clamped edge: margin ×1.4 on the weak (growth) side. 300 µm: 85 MPa, ×3.3. Geant4 L10: 0.28 against 0.27 d/µA. Order 300 µm.

Ogives: the wall

Al 200 µm buckles at 1.8 bar; 300 µm at 4.9. Be: 7 → 20 bar. His Cu 200 µm: 3.0 bar, just under CERN's ×3.

Heat is not the limit anywhere

≤ 70 K at 4 µA in every design. In the window it is the Ti rings and the 55 mm end piece that carry it (diamond 2 K, Ti rings 17 K, joint 2 K, end piece 25 K), not the diamond: braze or glue makes no difference.

Targets are consumables

Where the beam stops, H builds up: Cu blisters after ~5 days at 1 µA, Ta/Mo after ≥ 16 (§5); diamond is untested. At the 0.12–0.5 µA the 20 µm Li needs, plan 2–3 spares per campaign.

The real gates

Be (end piece, hemisphere, ogive): LNL safety approval and a Be-shop quote, 3–6 months. Everything else is the LNL workshop plus one CVD-diamond vendor (8–14 weeks).

Details

Sources and formulas: TARGET_OPTIONS §20 (ogive shells) and §21 (all designs); outputs practical_checks.csv, practical_flat_chamber.csv.

Decisions and what this does not settle

Decide

Build the 45° window on a Ø20 × 0.5 mm Be end piece: 0.22 d/µA, the flat design’s reach, no chamber, safe at 1 bar. A wide adapter is worse (0.37): the tube can only be made lighter, not moved out of view.

If Pierfrancesco keeps the shell, his ogive: Be 0.3 mm + Mo is the fastest target simulated (0.15 d/µA), Al 0.3 mm + Mo the cheap one (0.26); never Cu (0.94; his hemisphere 2.4).

Perpendicular only in a chamber (0.22); as a window, tilt it (0° costs ×1.36).

Not settled

The ogive’s flank sees 2.2× the Li: ×2.2 γ₀ per proton, but 28 % of it at 17.64 MeV (69 % at 1.03 MeV). Li thickness on the flank (or a mask to the tip) and the spot size are unknown.

A Be shell and a Be tube are custom parts (cost, lead time, safety: §20–21). Al 0.3 mm + Mo and a 0.25 mm Al or 0.5 mm CFRP tube are the fallbacks.

Window: Mo K x-rays in the MM, and H blistering of the Mo stop. Both need a bench test.

Reach is statistics only, at R(ATOMKI); no systematics.
